meaning: to stay positive and not show sadness during a difficult time
literal_translation: manter o ânimo e não desanimar
example: I know the exam was hard, but keep your chin up. You will get the next one.
origin: Refers to posture: lifting the chin instead of letting the head drop when someone feels low

wrong_meanings.meaning: to lift a heavy object using your head
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is a literal, physical action. The idiom is about attitude, not movement.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to eat a meal very quickly
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: Nothing in the idiom refers to food or eating. It is about emotional strength.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to speak very loudly in public
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with volume. It describes staying hopeful when things are hard.

explanation: 'Keep your chin up' means to stay positive and hopeful, especially when someone is sad, worried or disappointed. It is often said as encouragement.
